status: Analyst interpretations and testable mechanisms; not verified demographic or operational facts

cases.mechanism: Ordinary rental income with a small-household ownership fallback. Lower acquisition quantum can improve financing access; existing neighbourhood/transport utility must be shown in actual resident routines, not credited as a new catalyst.
cases.buyers: Primary: local working couple or small household valuing a real second room. Secondary: landlord buying supported whole-unit income. Do not borrow the buyer depth of 1050-sqft family units or generic KL professionals.
cases.comparables: 825/854-sqft Maxim expressions are primary type checks, with area/plan adjustments unresolved; 1050-sqft Maxim is a budget-and-extra-bedroom substitute, not a PSF anchor. Aster/Riana/Netizen are diagnostic alternatives only after exact type/price matching. KV13 is a capital opportunity-cost comparison, not a location comparable.
cases.project: Public rental/sale stock exists, but unique inventory, occupancy, lift performance, arrears and works are unverified. The project's mature lifecycle removes any automatic justification that weakness is merely first-VP release.
cases.unit: One bay may narrow two-car household adoption. Original second-bedroom dimensions, corridor exposure, actual station route, floor, facing, leaks and refurbishment inventory are unknown.
cases.exit: A cheaper compact unit could retain a financeable local household exit. The rival is an investor-dominated resale channel where rents alone set the bid and larger units compete near the same future budget.
cases.finance: Lease expiry, title transfer, lender valuation and parcel restrictions are not verified; 90%/35 years is solely the standard. Weak rent or fee increases can erase the thin current cushion.
cases.conclusion: Highest next-evidence priority among B01 additions, conditional on exact-price availability. Product preference is unproven; arithmetic challenges an automatic three-bedroom preference.
cases.next: Match original plan/bay/stack and effective price to the seller's exact parcel; confirm a whole-unit signed/renewed tenancy and itemised fee statement; obtain a recent matched resale plus competing three-bedroom budget check.

cases.mechanism: Compact urban rental convenience may command a rent premium, but that premium must cover the much higher entry quantum and continuing fit-out burden. Existing retail/rail proximity is not fresh appreciation.
cases.buyers: Primary: working couple/single needing a separate study/guest room in the Maluri routine. Secondary: compact owner household. International-school or large-family demand is not transferable to 750 sqft by assertion.
cases.comparables: Other 750-sqft Lavile units are primary; EkoCheras duplex, M Vertica 850-sqft and Cochrane products are diagnostic total-budget/routine choices, not interchangeable rents or PSF. Premium furnishing needs explicit inventory matching.
cases.project: Developer identity is available; current MC accounts, actual collected fees, lift/circulation conditions, occupancy and unique resale inventory are not. Rent listings do not establish an owner premium.
cases.unit: One bay, actual usable area, privacy, neighbouring stacks and mixed-use circulation require inspection. Furnished sale does not prove equivalent quality to the rental lead.
cases.exit: Future small-household buyers must choose this unit over larger same-budget homes. An attractive tenant rent can coexist with weak owner willingness-to-pay; terminal price cannot be justified by a tenant's income alone.
cases.finance: Do not assume property type labels settle land/title, tariffs, financing or remaining capital works. Higher price increases cash exposure even with a positive standard proxy.
cases.conclusion: Conditional standard surplus, below preferred 6% gross and negative annual carry. Investigate after the more affordable B01 compact case; no validated living-quality superiority.
cases.next: Verify same-package achieved rent and renewal; establish effective 750-sqft clearing evidence and competing larger homes at terminal budget; obtain fee/MC/works and exact-unit condition pack.

cases.mechanism: Possible apparent cheapness comes from unit-cohort differences and local rental economics. It is not validated mispricing merely because the 850-sqft ask is below a project-wide median.
cases.buyers: Primary: local small household with car-based Cheras Selatan routines. Secondary: local working tenants. MRT-family/central-KL tenant depth cannot be borrowed without door-to-door evidence.
cases.comparables: Type A 850-sqft Akasa is primary; 1152/1155-sqft units are different cohorts. C180/Balakong products and local landed quantum are functional substitution investigations, not adopted fair-value comparables.
cases.project: Developer text establishes the two-bedroom-plus-utility type. Current occupancy, investor supply, management recovery and common-property works are unknown. A temporary supply-release story needs dates and absorption evidence.
cases.unit: Two bays are advertised but bay rights/usability are not checked. Utility is not an approved third bedroom. Noise, access queues, ventilation and exact block remain unresolved.
cases.exit: An owner exit requires preference for this smaller high-rise over local larger homes. Weak rent and larger competing supply may persist even after any temporary release ends.
cases.finance: Current standard shortfall remains under the common baseline. No actual bank value/title/works evidence. A lower quoted price cannot rescue unknown rights or financing.
cases.conclusion: Lowest research tier while standard shortfall persists. Continue as a mispricing investigation only on measurable rent, effective-price or supply evidence.
cases.next: Obtain matched 850-sqft transfers rather than project median; verify achieved whole-unit rent and fee; confirm unique competing inventory/absorption and exact plan/bays before advancing.

cases.mechanism: Proximity to a rail catchment can lower commuting friction only if the real pedestrian route works. Product quality and price must convert that access into durable household preference.
cases.buyers: Primary: rail-using couple/small household able to use the original two-bedroom plan. Secondary: nearby local owner. Generic TOD investor demand is not independent owner demand.
cases.comparables: Same 847-sqft You Vista type is primary; You City III/Netizen and local older family condos are substitution leads with different size/lifecycle. No equal-PSF assumption.
cases.project: Multi-unit advertising and repeated broker supply do not reveal unique stock or turnover. Common-property operations, resident mix and current supply competition remain unknown.
cases.unit: Original 847-sqft plan and 850-sqft rental proxy are not yet reconciled; two bays and route/entrance, lift waits and stack exposure need verification.
cases.exit: Exit would depend on a household choosing usable access and layout at the future quantum. Nearby compact and three-bedroom supply can cap a premium even where location demand is sound.
cases.finance: RM450k is a starting-price lead, not a parcel quote. Title/financeability and rate/valuation stress remain unresolved; no catalyst-funded carrying plan accepted.
cases.conclusion: Lowest research tier under current standard shortfall. This is an access/price hypothesis, not a confirmed weak project.
cases.next: Resolve exact sale parcel/starting-price terms and original plan; verify achieved rent/fee for the same type; test station route and recent owner-oriented matched resales.

cases.mechanism: Investigate whether local family utility supports high-rise ownership where landed options influence budget choices. Current low rental support is evidence against assuming a location story translates into income.
cases.buyers: Primary: local household needing three usable rooms and two bays. Secondary: price-sensitive local tenant. Sungai Long institutional demand cannot simply be assigned to Mahkota.
cases.comparables: 1161-sqft Emerald in Mahkota is primary. Teluk Kumbar Emerald is rejected geography; 1130-sqft auction lots have different motive/rights. Local low-rise/landed and potential Desa Tiara supply are diagnostic choices.
cases.project: Old transaction cohort and newer sale ads leave present price discovery unresolved. No current management/maintenance evidence; project scale is not a governance score. Future brochure supply is not counted as delivered inventory.
cases.unit: Actual layout, bay arrangement, condition and block privacy are unverified. Larger furnished rental advertisements do not prove this smaller partial unit can achieve the same rent.
cases.exit: Owner exit depends on budget-sensitive families accepting strata living over credible local landed/low-rise choices. The resale ceiling may be set by functional substitutes, not replacement cost.
cases.finance: No use of auction reserve as achievable vacant-possession purchase. Title, arrears, fee and lending evidence missing; current carry deficit requires funded holding rather than hopeful booster uplift.
cases.conclusion: Lowest research tier. No current G0 discount thesis or reason to promote above income-supported alternatives.
cases.next: Find recent matched ordinary transfers with true Mahkota identity; verify 1161-sqft achieved rents and MC dues; test same-budget local household substitutes and future competing delivery status.

cases.mechanism: A more affordable expression can improve access to a product with an existing living-quality thesis, but quality does not automatically transmit into enough rent or resale premium.
cases.buyers: Primary: small family prioritising liveability and three usable rooms. Secondary: long-term local tenant. Buyers of 2497-sqft large units are a separate budget/product universe.
cases.comparables: 916-sqft Windows is primary; the historical 2497-sqft case is a product-expression contrast only. BTHO alternatives and landed options require total-budget comparison, not pooled PSF.
cases.project: Developer/product evidence is inherited, not fresh proof of current management. Common-property finances, repairs, operating quality and unique inventory need new evidence.
cases.unit: Selected sale has one bay; rental has two tandem bays and map-address uncertainty. These differences weaken the rent transfer. Room dimensions, actual privacy and irreversible exposure uninspected.
cases.exit: Quality-oriented family buyers may pay for utility, but at the required exit budget could prefer larger or landed alternatives. A rental investor cannot be presumed to fund the owner's desired premium.
cases.finance: Current standard shortfall is substantial even at smaller entry quantum. No verified management invoice or bank terms; five-year carrying burden must be funded.
cases.conclusion: Lowest income-research tier while retaining a separate living-quality investigation. No permanent exclusion for future market change.
cases.next: Resolve rental identity, bay and size match; obtain current management/works and unit condition evidence; test actual family resale behaviour versus local budget substitutes.

cases.mechanism: Compact quantum may access southwest-KL work routines, but portal presentation and price conflicts can create artificial cheapness. Existing connectivity needs a usable route and timetable, not a distance badge.
cases.buyers: Primary: local working couple/small household. Secondary: ordinary tenant needing two rooms. Demand for larger nearby OUG/Taman Desa family homes is not automatically a two-bedroom exit.
cases.comparables: Same 725-sqft Citizen 2 is primary; 883-sqft Citizen 2 and Petalz/OUG alternatives are budget/function checks. Citizen and Citizen 2 must remain separate; developer identity corrected with primary source E52.
cases.project: Public stock is visible, but listing count is not unique inventory. Portal prose contradicts its own developer/blocks/parking metadata. No operating conclusions adopted from that boilerplate.
cases.unit: One advertised bay conflicts with generic two-bay project copy; parcel documents control. Exact layout, furnishing, high-floor exposure and access/circulation unknown.
cases.exit: Future owner demand requires a usable second room and acceptable daily route. Larger local units and newer compact supply could cap resale; claimed portal search preference is not financed buyer depth.
cases.finance: RM400k headline was rejected because body says RM470k. Selected RM430k remains an ask. Current conservative rent scenario has a shortfall; approved financing and valuations unresolved.
cases.conclusion: Lowest tier at RM1900 base rent; recent RM2000 asks can reverse the standard sign but do not clear G0 or prove achieved rent. Positive arithmetic is fragile.
cases.next: Obtain a clean exact-unit net quote and original plan/bay inventory; verify signed rent/fees; obtain matched 725-sqft resales and total-budget 883-sqft alternatives.

cases.mechanism: Lower-quantum rail-linked housing may attract ordinary tenants, but apparent discount to an agent's bank-value claim is not evidence. Furnishing-specific rents and lease/operations matter.
cases.buyers: Primary: small working household using the Ara Damansara routine. Secondary: income buyer at demonstrated rent. Premium landed/Tropicana owner preferences are not transferable by district name.
cases.comparables: 864-sqft two-bedroom Pacific Place is primary. 529-sqft marketed two-bedroom units, 708-sqft studio and dual-key larger types are excluded from direct rents. D'aman Crimson/Puncak Nusa Kelana are local substitute investigations.
cases.project: Project name includes commercial centre but the selected use is residential service-residence marketing. Mixed-use operations, MC financial health, competing inventory and residential lease terms unresolved.
cases.unit: Selected furnished sale lacks a verified bay entitlement. Exact second bedroom, noise, circulation, ventilation and actual station access cannot be inferred from photos not inspected.
cases.exit: Modest-quantum local buyers may provide an exit if lease, condition and recurring fees remain acceptable. Strong location access alone cannot prevent product ageing or a narrow owner pool.
cases.finance: The cheaper source conflicts at RM330k/RM338k and uses illustrative photos; it is not an adopted discount. Lease expiry/lender terms are unknown; 90%/35-year model is conditional.
cases.conclusion: Middle evidence priority with only RM26/month assumed standard cushion. Rent/fee revisions readily move it to lowest tier. No 25%-below-market claim accepted.
cases.next: Verify parcel plan/bays/lease and effective sale terms; establish achieved furnished rent and actual dues; inspect recent matched residential transfers and current common-property works.

cases.mechanism: Three rooms at a moderate quantum may retain a local household fallback. Its benefit must outweigh one-bay constraints, furnishing costs and mature-building capital works.
cases.buyers: Primary: local family needing three real rooms. Secondary: local tenants/income buyer. Do not import Desa ParkCity prestige or premium Mont Kiara expatriate demand into Kepong.
cases.comparables: 1074-sqft First Residence is primary. 930/937, 1107/1109 and 1182/1184-sqft versions are different cohorts; neighbouring Herz/Kepongmas/older landed are functional alternatives subject to rights/eligibility.
cases.project: Portal automated 51.58% yield and mixed-size decline were rejected. Current governance, reserve adequacy, lift performance and special levies are unknown; age creates an investigation need, not proven deterioration.
cases.unit: Sale partial versus rent furnished requires an actual upgrade budget; one bay may be decisive for families. Advertiser photos may be illustrative. Noise, stack and maintenance uninspected.
cases.exit: Family resale depth could be stronger than a studio's, but the next buyer must finance the terminal budget while comparing two-bay alternatives. No actual owner-occupier ratio obtained.
cases.finance: Lease expiry/transfer, bank value and low-downpayment scheme terms unknown. The mature-building works shock is material relative to the thin base surplus.
cases.conclusion: Priority challenger to compact two-bedroom assumptions, not a confirmed quality winner. Base meets 6% only approximately and annual carry is negative.
cases.next: Match effective ordinary sale and plan/bay rights; verify furnished achieved rent plus itemised upgrade/dues; obtain MC works reserve and recent household-led resales versus two-bay substitutes.

cases.mechanism: Premium mixed-use convenience can support higher rent but also a much higher purchase price. School-neighbourhood prestige and a future MRT label do not establish one-bedroom owner demand.
cases.buyers: Primary: single/couple professional tenant choosing local convenience. Secondary: one-bedroom owner or yield investor. School-family demand for large apartments is a false borrowed buyer universe.
cases.comparables: Same residential 696-sqft component is primary. 710/788-sqft types, hotel suites and Arcoris commercial/residential components require separate identities. Larger Mont Kiara family condos are budget-choice diagnostics.
cases.project: Component identity and current operations must be verified. High advertised rents are not occupancy, renewed corporate leases or sustainable premium. Future MRT construction can also create interim disruption.
cases.unit: One bedroom may limit long-term household adoption; exact stack, parking, privacy, noise and hotel/serviced circulation unknown. No aesthetic quality score from unviewed imagery.
cases.exit: At future high quantum, an owner may choose a larger older family unit. A higher-paying tenant does not prove a high-price resale buyer; investor valuation remains tied to sustainable net income.
cases.finance: Selected price is RM850k; older RM770k link redirected and is not an executable alternative. Confirm strata use, permitted letting, bank valuation and finance term.
cases.conclusion: Lowest current-income priority. Premium product remains a diagnostic countercase; no structural Reject from insufficient yield alone.
cases.next: Verify exact residential component/title/fee and effective price; obtain ordinary long-tenure achieved/renewed rent; test one-bedroom financed resales against same-budget larger alternatives.

cases.mechanism: Central access and established amenities can support rent, while old-building financing, works and effective-price incentives may erase apparent value. No new-booster uplift assumed.
cases.buyers: Primary: city-centre worker/couple wanting an ordinary whole-unit tenancy. Secondary: local compact owner. Tourist room-night revenue and generic city-centre prestige are excluded as independent owner evidence.
cases.comparables: Exact 660-sqft original one-bedroom is primary; 650/659/680/707 are near-size diagnostics pending plans. Angkasa Impian 1 and 1100–1500-sqft family units remain separate.
cases.project: Portal freehold narrative contradicts leasehold listing/transaction metadata. Current MC accounts, repairs, lifts, security and permitted tenancy pattern unknown.
cases.unit: Original one-bedroom and one bay need title/plan confirmation; modified layouts and room counts differ across ads. Night noise, slope/route and common circulation not inspected.
cases.exit: Next buyer may prefer newer compact stock or a larger nearby older unit. Sparse old transfers cannot establish current liquidity; carry-funded exit delay must be possible.
cases.finance: Cashback/full-loan marketing means headline RM440k is not validated economic consideration. Current standard balance is approximately zero before all other costs; lease/financing uncertainty material.
cases.conclusion: Lowest tier under the negative base result; tiny sign changes do not establish value. Higher rent must be evidenced with the same original unit and ordinary tenure.
cases.next: Resolve effective consideration, title/lease and original plan; verify comparable achieved whole-unit rent/fees; obtain current MC works and matched resale evidence with real exit time.

cases.mechanism: A low advertised entry and ordinary two-bedroom rent create a possible income lead, but the price instrument is internally inconsistent. The analytical task is to establish that an actual sale opportunity exists before rewarding yield.
cases.buyers: Primary: local working couple/small household. Secondary: ordinary tenants linked to genuine local routines. Student demand, room partitions and family demand for larger PV layouts are not interchangeable.
cases.comparables: 900-sqft two-bedroom PV21 is primary. 1040/1325-sqft three-bedroom stock and other PV developments must remain distinct; marketed 900-sqft three-bedroom partitions cannot set the two-bedroom base rent.
cases.project: Current governance, high-rise operations, resident mix, true rental inventory and competing delivery are unknown. Portal MRT proximity is not accepted as existing operational utility.
cases.unit: Original plan, approved bedroom count, two advertised bays and exact tower/unit require confirmation. No partition premium or visual quality judgement adopted.
cases.exit: An owner fallback needs evidence that ordinary households buy this type, not only investors converting rooms. Weak owner depth could keep sale values tied to marginal net yield.
cases.finance: Sale header/RM310k body but 'for rent' wording keeps consideration unresolved. G0 stop is especially strong. A low scenario price is not a financeable offer.
cases.conclusion: Identity/price-resolution queue only; not eligible for the positive-income shortlist until the conflict is resolved. Conditional 6%-plus arithmetic cannot promote it.
cases.next: Resolve sale versus rent and obtain clean net parcel quote; verify original plan/bays and achieved ordinary rent/dues; establish current matched ordinary residential transfers and owner-buyer motive.

cases.mechanism: At the advertised quantum, two bedrooms and two bays could serve ordinary local households as well as tenants. Existing retail/employment access may support utility; it is not an automatic new catalyst.
cases.buyers: Primary: Puchong working couple/small family with two vehicles. Secondary: income buyer. Broad Puchong landed-family demand or generic transit investors cannot automatically supply the exit.
cases.comparables: 881-sqft Skypod is primary. Registered 861-sqft records need strata-area resolution. RM410k high-floor/corner example differs from selected RM380k. 1033/1248-sqft family types and local landed quantum are budget substitutes.
cases.project: Official developer source distinguishes retail/office stock. Residential operations, unique supply, lift performance, resident selection and MC works are unverified; nearby retail does not prove project strength.
cases.unit: Two bays may improve household fit if rights and manoeuvrability hold. Actual facing, road noise, unit defects and pedestrian route require evidence.
cases.exit: Small-household ownership fallback is plausible and could challenge Maxim at the same price. The countercase is persistent price discount caused by operations, access or weak genuine secondary demand.
cases.finance: Six public residential transfers across a rolling 13-month period are too few/mixed to validate fast exit. Current 90% financing, exact title and cash requirements remain assumptions.
cases.conclusion: Highest-priority cross-region challenger with Maxim. No final ordering: RM20 assumed monthly balance difference is smaller than unresolved rent/fee uncertainty.
cases.next: Confirm RM380k exact-unit net quote/bays/condition against RM410k alternative; verify furnished achieved rent and dues; reconcile 861/881-sqft ordinary transfers and household exit behaviour.

cases.mechanism: Low acquisition quantum and an evidenced institutional accommodation channel can support ordinary income without appreciation. The mechanism can exist even with narrower family-owner appeal, but it must survive substitute accommodation and turnover costs.
cases.buyers: Primary tenant hypothesis: individual student/worker or couple needing a small entire unit. Primary exit hypothesis: an income buyer; secondary compact owner is unproven. Large-family owner depth must not be borrowed.
cases.comparables: 450-sqft Solstice within the correct residential component is primary. 750/893/980-sqft units, hotel/office stock, auction reserves and Philippine namesakes are excluded. Kanvas/Antara and other university accommodation are demand substitutes, not equal property valuations.
cases.project: University listing supports a channel and its other options undermine a captive-demand assumption. No enrolment-to-occupancy conversion, unique inventory, churn, management or collected-rent evidence obtained.
cases.unit: Marketed one-bedroom, residential use, original plan and exact parking remain unresolved. Furnished stock still requires appliance replacement and management; 450 sqft limits household expansion.
cases.exit: Income-led exit may be viable at an evidenced yield but is exposed to financing and competing cheap supply. Owner diversity is weaker as a hypothesis, not proven absent. The positive gross yield cannot substitute for resale evidence.
cases.finance: Small capital quantum lowers nominal exposure but not title, parcel-use, lease/financeability or works risk. A RM30k levy is large relative to price; actual valuation and LTV may differ.
cases.conclusion: High-priority counterexample investigation alongside household-oriented leads; not promoted to best asset by 7.2% gross. Lowest base annual deficit still rests on unverified fees, rent and occupancy.
cases.next: Verify parcel residential rights/plan/bay and effective RM200k availability; establish renewed whole-unit rent, collection history and actual dues/turnover costs; obtain matched ordinary resale and financed exit-buyer evidence.
